# Loom Agent V1.1 — Full Agent Context

> Use this file to orient a coding agent before modifying Loom. Source code and tests remain authoritative.

## Purpose and scope

Loom is a CLI-first **durable multi-agent runtime** for developer work. V1.1 exposes a public SDK and package graph while preserving persisted agent identity, delegation, messages, leases, structured results, artifacts, decisions, and recovery state in SQLite.

V1.1 supports a controller-oriented daemon, authenticated control plane, scheduler, and outbound remote workers. It is still not a distributed consensus or storage system; HA, mesh/P2P, NAT traversal, Redis/Kafka, vector memory, and cloud orchestration remain out of scope.

The milestone-specific V0.4 sections below are retained as historical context. Prefer current package manifests, README, and tests when behavior differs.

## Requirements and checks

```bash
bun install
npm run build
npm test
npm run eval
npm run loom -- run "create a release note" --max-agents 2
```

Node.js 22+ provides `node:sqlite`. Bun is supported for development and `bun:sqlite`.

## Packages

- `@loom-agent/core`: lifecycle, role, message, result, lease, artifact, memory, and trace contracts.
- `@loom-agent/state`: migrations v1–v5, transactions, durable state, and the tool ledger.
- `@loom-agent/planner`: deterministic plans, dependencies, V0.3 verified execution, and graph recovery.
- `@loom-agent/coordinator`: roles, child lifecycle, delegation, A2A, context isolation, bounded execution, recovery, and cancellation.
- `@loom-agent/tools`: registry, native tools, permission/approval middleware, idempotency, timeout, path safety, and result limits.
- `@loom-agent/providers`: mock and OpenAI-compatible adapters.
- `@loom-agent/context`: priority-based context compiler.
- `@loom-agent/skills`: project skill discovery.
- `@loom-agent/mcp`: local stdio MCP adapter.
- `@loom-agent/runtime`: legacy `AgentLoop` compatibility path.
- `@loom-agent/evals`: six V0.3 regression scenarios and eight V0.4 coordination scenarios.
- `@loom-agent/cli`: config, command parsing, service wiring, and output.

Keep reusable coordination out of the CLI. Preserve the V0.3 runtime unless a compatibility change is required.

## Agent and role model

An agent stores:

```text
id parentAgentId rootAgentId role goal task status result error timestamps
```

Roles are `planner`, `researcher`, `coder`, `reviewer`, `tester`, and `general`. Built-in definitions contain instructions, allowed tools, and completion criteria. `.loom/agents/<role>.md` can replace instructions. Role policy narrows project permissions and never bypasses `ask` or `deny`.

Root and child statuses:

```text
created running waiting paused recovering completed failed cancelled stopped
```

Default role tools:

```text
planner/researcher/reviewer/tester: read_file shell
coder/general: read_file write_file shell
```

## Coordination lifecycle

```text
root goal
-> persist root, plan, graph
-> find runnable tasks
-> atomically create child + delegation
-> acquire task lease
-> compile isolated role/task context
-> execute through provider and ToolExecutor
-> atomically persist result + result message
-> deliver summary to root exactly once
-> acknowledge result and update graph
-> verify, repair, or complete
```

`agents.maxConcurrent` or `--max-agents` bounds the batch size. Default concurrency is 2.

## Delegation and leases

Delegation statuses are:

```text
created assigned running waiting completed failed cancelled
```

Each task can store `ownerAgentId`, `leaseId`, and `leaseExpiresAt`. `task_leases` retains history. Lease acquisition and task ownership update in one SQLite transaction. Another agent cannot take an unexpired lease.

Creating a child and delegation is atomic. Persisting a structured result, completing the delegation, updating the child, and creating the result A2A message is atomic. Result ids are unique per delegation.

## Local A2A bus

Messages are distinct from provider chat messages. Fields include id, root, sender, recipient, type, JSON payload, visibility, and delivery/acknowledgement timestamps.

Types:

```text
request response status artifact error cancel
```

The bus supports send, receive, acknowledge, and list. It rejects cross-root messages. Stable result message ids and acknowledgement prevent duplicate parent consumption.

## Context and memory isolation

A child receives its role, assigned goal/task, a concise parent summary, visible memory, allowed tools, and messages addressed to it. Do not include every agent's history or memory.

Memory scopes:

```text
agent root-task project
```

Visibility:

```text
private parent-visible team-visible
```

Project-level writes require explicit package policy. Semantic/vector memory is not implemented.

## Failure, review, and approval

Failure policies remain:

```text
retryable non_retryable blocked needs_approval needs_human
```

Retryable child failures may be reassigned within budget. Reviewer rejection reopens the nearest implementation task and resets downstream verification. Decisions persist in `coordination_decisions` and traces.

An approval record includes child id, role, task, tool, normalized input, argument summary, and reason. Approve or deny, then resume the root. Loom reuses the waiting child.

```bash
npm run loom -- approvals <root-id>
npm run loom -- approve <request-id>
npm run loom -- resume <root-id>
```

## Recovery and duplicate prevention

`resume` reconstructs the root tree, plan, delegations, task ownership, leases, messages, results, checkpoints, artifacts, approvals, and tool ledger.

Recovery invariants:

- Persisted child results are delivered and acknowledged once.
- Unfinished work reuses the existing child/delegation.
- Interrupted leases are released before the same child continues.
- Durable tool-call ids reuse `succeeded` results.
- `executing` or `unknown` tool calls are not silently replayed.
- Approval resumes the child that requested it.
- Cancellation releases leases and cancels active descendants.

## SQLite migration v5

Migrations v1–v4 remain unchanged. Migration 5:

- adds parent/root/role/goal columns to `agents`;
- adds owner/lease columns to `plan_tasks`;
- adds type/visibility to artifacts and approval/trace correlation columns;
- creates `delegations`, `agent_messages`, `agent_results`, `task_leases`, `scoped_memory`, and `coordination_decisions`;
- backfills V0.3 agents as root general agents and old traces with their root id.

The migration runs transactionally and has a V0.3 database upgrade test.

## CLI

```text
run <goal> [--max-agents N] [--max-tasks N]
ps
agents [root-id]
inspect <agent-id>
agent inspect <agent-id>
agent cancel <agent-id>
resume <root-id>
delegations <agent-id>
messages <agent-id>
trace <agent-id>
approvals [agent-id]
approve <request-id>
deny <request-id>
skills / tools / memory / config
```

`ps` lists roots. `agents` lists child identities. Root `trace` returns the correlated tree timeline. Add `--json` for structured output.

## Trace correlation

Trace events support:

```text
rootAgentId agentId parentAgentId taskId delegationId messageId toolCallId checkpointId
```

Coordination events include `agent.spawned`, `delegation.created`, `message.sent`, `task.leased`, `result.handoff`, `message.acknowledged`, `task.reassigned`, and cancellation/failure/completion variants.

## Evaluation contract

The original six scenarios remain regression coverage. V0.4 adds parent-to-coder, researcher-to-coder, coder-reviewer repair, bounded parallelism, child crash/resume, parent crash before result consumption, hierarchical cancellation, and child approval/resume.

All scenarios run without API keys and use deterministic in-memory workers. They validate orchestration, not model intelligence.

## Security boundaries

Every child goes through `ToolRegistry`, `ToolExecutor`, workspace path checks, shell timeout/output limits, role restrictions, project permissions, approval policy, idempotency ledger, artifact tracking, and traces.

Loom is not a sandbox. Context visibility is not an OS boundary. Traces do not receive general secret redaction. Run untrusted work in a container, VM, or restricted account.

## Known limitations

- Local process and local SQLite only.
- Rule-based plans and role selection.
- No provider streaming and one tool round.
- “Targeted” verification currently runs the full Vitest suite.
- Diff review is structural, not semantic.
- No network A2A, remote workers, daemon, scheduler, or distributed queue.
- No vector memory or embeddings.
- Role model routing and full Markdown role policy are not implemented.
- Artifact tracking is declared, not a complete filesystem diff.
